A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GATEAU research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. The new Table 14 contains a local labeling inconsistency, but no reading or extraction gap prevents comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, human evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds selection-overlap measurements, a mixed-quality training comparison, and selected-sample examples in Appendices I.5, I.6, and J.

M1.justification: The HMG and CAM components, normalization, weighted sample ranking, and supervised fine-tuning objective remain unchanged in Equations (1)-(7). Mixed-quality training is tested as an alternative in Appendix I.6, without changing the proposed GATEAU procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongAlign and ShareGPT and retain LongBench, LongBench-Chat, MT-Bench, needle retrieval, and the debate-summary case study. The added analyses reuse existing data and tasks. Qwen2.5-1M is cited as a future possibility, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Appendix I.6 adds a comparison against training on the top 5% plus bottom 5% of scored samples. The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Table 13 reuses CaR and the existing Cherry Selection baseline, called 'Cherry LLM' there, for overlap analysis.

E3.justification: v3 adds an overlap metric for top-10% selections under Limited Short Instruction Data Settings and a top-10% versus top-5%-plus-bottom-5% training comparison under both settings. Appendix J selects the highest- and lowest-scoring examples for inspection. Existing benchmark protocols, model configurations, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices I.5-I.6 add focused checks of whether GATEAU selects different samples from existing baselines and whether mixing high- and low-scoring data helps training. Appendix J adds a two-example quality case study. Earlier ablations, sensitivity studies, retrieval tests, and OOD analysis remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly specifies that GPT-4 scores the 200 selected samples twice and the scores are averaged. v2 already identifies the 100 highest- and 100 lowest-scoring samples and reports repeated benchmark scoring, but lacks this explicit repetition detail for the characteristics analysis. This disclosure does not establish an increase in runs; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1-12 and existing plots retain their results. New Table 13 reports 12% overlap with Cherry LLM and 5% with CaR. Table 14 adds comparison rows with LongBench-Chat scores of 53.6 and 55.6 alongside retained GATEAU scores of 55.4 and 58.0. Its 'w/o Mixed-Quality Data' label conflicts with Appendix I.6's mixed-data description, leaving the row attribution ambiguous. Figure 18 adds qualitative examples.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions, Equations (1)-(7), and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The new discussion of 'orthogonality' is an empirical interpretation and introduces no formal definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: selecting samples rich in long-range dependencies through HMG and CAM and improving alignment using a selected subset, including the claim about using only 10% of the data. The appendix additions supply further support without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit limitation when inputs exceed the base model's context window. It interprets low selection overlap as evidence of different patterns, the mixed-quality trial as supporting top-ranked selection, and the new examples as showing better faithfulness and fluency. Appendix C also adds literature-based arguments for the reliability of GPT-4 judging.

D1.justification: Appendices I.5-I.6 document concrete subset-construction recipes for the added analyses: top-10% selections for overlap and top-5%-plus-bottom-5% samples for mixed-quality training. Existing implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, evaluator versions, runtime reporting, and the promised code/data/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen2.5-1M technical report by Yang et al. (2025), expands discussion of GPT-4 evaluation reliability using existing Bai et al. and Zheng et al. references, and discusses potential complementarity with selection baselines in Appendix I.5. The main related-work section and overall novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Local edits pluralize 'Sample' in the title, update one author affiliation, correct the Figure 4 cross-reference, and rewrite parts of the evaluation descriptions. The appendix roadmap gains I.5, I.6, and J, and Limitations becomes unnumbered. The main narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 13-14 and Figure 18, relocates Table 12, and reformats the retained OOD example in Figure 17 with smaller text and greater separation between responses. Existing plots and table bodies remain unchanged; the Table 2 caption is lightly reordered.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency by explicitly stating the context-window limitation and repeated scoring for the existing sample-characteristics analysis. The overlap diagnostic also makes the selection behavior more inspectable. The added validation has limits: Table 14's label conflicts with Appendix I.6, and Figure 18 omits the input contexts needed to check its faithfulness claim. These local weaknesses limit the gains while leaving the original method and empirical evidence intact.
